Single-cell and spatial transcriptome analyses unveil that MYH11 links stemness to immunotherapy resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.

Combining single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, the authors identify a MYH11-high subpopulation of cancer stem-like cells in non-small cell lung cancer that is linked to immunotherapy resistance. The work implicates MYH11 as a marker connecting tumor stemness to immune evasion, suggesting a potential target or biomarker for stratifying patients who may fail immunotherapy.

Spatial transcriptomics reveals PDIA6 as a tumor-intrinsic driver of mesenchymal plasticity and vascular microenvironment remodeling in glioblastoma.

Using spatial transcriptomics, this study identifies PDIA6 as a tumor-intrinsic factor in glioblastoma that promotes mesenchymal plasticity and remodels the vascular microenvironment, potentially creating protective perivascular niches. The findings link PDIA6 to malignant-endothelial crosstalk and suggest it as a candidate driver of therapy resistance in GBM.

Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.

The authors analyzed a pan-pediatric single-cell RNA-seq atlas of 266 samples across 22 pediatric solid tumor types to identify shared developmental gene expression programs. They found that pediatric sarcomas exhibit lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs, and used these programs to nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs as potential therapeutic targets. This work demonstrates how single-cell atlases can reveal convergent vulnerabilities in low-mutation-burden pediatric tumors.

HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues.

HOMED is a new computational framework for DNA methylation deconvolution that accounts for hierarchical relationships among related cell types and uses single-cell RNA-seq plus paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data to optimize CpG signatures. This improves the accuracy of estimating cell-type proportions from bulk methylation data, which is important for epigenome-wide association studies where cellular heterogeneity confounds results.

Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.

This review categorizes 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency (differentiation potential) from static scRNA-seq data into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based approaches. The authors show these methods rest on different, sometimes conflicting assumptions, and analyze them within a unified mathematical framework. The work provides guidance for choosing appropriate potency-estimation tools and highlights conceptual disagreements in the field.

CellMarker 3.0: an updated resource of manually curated and computationally predicted cell markers in human/mouse and interactive web tools for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis.

CellMarker 3.0 is an updated database that combines manually curated, experimentally validated cell marker genes with computationally predicted markers for many cell types in human and mouse tissues. The release adds substantial new content (274 tissues, 1,877 cell types, 64,040 markers, and over 1.2 million tissue-cell type-marker entries) and introduces interactive web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics data. It serves as a practical reference and analysis platform for cell-type annotation in single-cell and spatial studies.

spaTransfer: transfer learning for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data using non-negative matrix factorization.

spaTransfer is a new computational method that uses non-negative matrix factorization to transfer cell type or spatial domain annotations from a reference single-cell or spatial transcriptomics atlas to a new target sample, even when the two datasets differ in resolution or were generated on different experimental platforms. This addresses a key challenge in leveraging large-scale atlases for annotating new spatial data.

Denoising single-cell ATAC-seq data with Shannon entropy.

The authors introduce a Shannon entropy-based method for denoising scATAC-seq data by identifying and filtering out low-quality droplets, such as empty droplets or those containing damaged nuclei and cellular debris. Unlike existing approaches that rely on read depth or predefined genomic features, this method uses the information content of the chromatin accessibility landscape itself to distinguish high-quality nuclei. This helps prevent noisy reads from distorting downstream analyses and obscuring rare cell populations.

CellWHISPER disentangles direct cell-cell communication from structural proximity.

CellWHISPER is a new computational framework for inferring direct, contact-dependent cell-cell communication (gap junctions and ligand-receptor signaling) from spatial transcriptomics data. It addresses a key problem in existing tools—high error rates caused by confounding spatial structure in cell types and gene expression—by using a statistical procedure that controls for these confounders. Closed-form significance scores make the method scalable to large datasets.

Thermodynamic Quality Control Reshapes Spatially Resolved Metabolic Flux Predictions in Prostate Cancer.

This preprint integrates spatial transcriptomics from twelve annotated regions of a single prostate tumor with the Human-GEM genome-scale metabolic model using an E-Flux framework, adding nutrient constraints, explicit cycle certification, and loopless flux variability analysis. The authors show that unconstrained models admit thermodynamically infeasible cycles (TICs) that distort spatially resolved metabolic flux predictions, and that thermodynamic quality control reshapes those predictions across normal, inflamed, and Gleason 3+3/3+4 regions. The work highlights a methodological pitfall in spatial flux inference and offers a corrective workflow.

X-SPEAR: An Extensible Framework for Spatial Panel Evaluation and Refinement.

X-SPEAR is a framework for designing and evaluating targeted spatial transcriptomics gene panels, addressing the problem that genes chosen from scRNA-seq references are often detected in fewer cells in spatial assays, with gene-specific dropout. Its marker-selection method, DART, learns short Boolean gene rules and retains multiple gene-disjoint rules per cell type to improve rare-cell typing robustness. The tool helps researchers build and validate Xenium panels more reliably.

This links predicted cell-cell communication to clinical outcomes, showing that single-cell-derived communication networks carry prognostic signal and can be prioritized for survival relevance.

SVC: A Vision Transformer-based Spatially and Virtually Embedded Cell Model for Deciphering Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomic Heterogeneity.

SVC is a Vision Transformer-based model that learns subcellular transcript localization patterns directly from subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics data, representing each gene's localization as an image patch with other genes in the same cell as context. This enables scalable profiling of subcellular transcript heterogeneity across tissues and disease states, addressing a major gap in studying subcellular spatial organization at scale.

CQRM: A Composite Quantile Regression Model for Differential Expression Analysis of Non-Coding RNA Count Data.

The authors propose CQRM, a composite quantile regression framework for differential expression analysis of non-coding RNA count data. It uses jittering to handle the discrete nature of counts and tests across multiple quantiles adaptively, addressing the low expression and high variability typical of ncRNAs. This provides an alternative to standard mean-based DE methods for this challenging data type.

Deep-learning-driven tumor microenvironment profiling improves immunotherapy response prediction.

Topology-adjusted knockout (TAKO): interpretable in silico single-gene knockout ranking on wild-type single-cell gene regulatory networks.

TAKO is a computational framework that predicts the effects of knocking out individual genes using only wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data, without needing any knockout-specific training. It works by simulating a strict 'cut-in-and-out' intervention on gene regulatory network dynamics and measuring how much the network's stationary propagation profile changes. This enables interpretable ranking of single-gene knockout impacts at low computational cost.

Immune-chondrocyte ligand-receptor axes in osteoarthritis: microenvironmental control of inflammation, matrix remodeling, and chondrocyte fate.

A curvilinear coordinate flatmap for visualizing hippocampal structure and development.

The authors developed a computational workflow that unfolds the curved, topographically complex hippocampal formation into a flat 2D map using curvilinear coordinates derived from solving the Laplacian equation. This flatmap preserves geodesic relationships and laminar boundaries, making it easier to visualize and analyze subregional, laminar, and connectivity patterns in mouse hippocampal data registered to the Common Coordinate Framework. The approach offers a standardized reference for studying hippocampal structure and development.
